correctness.summary: The fixed-q extension was checked directly against En Gad's v1 proof. Section 8 explicitly lists codes over a fixed larger alphabet as open. In the source bubble lemma, the only binary-specific use of 1-d is that each run boundary differs from d, so arbitrary q-ary left and right boundary symbols work even when unequal. In the source counting lemma, each bubble header records the edited bit and at most one extra bit is needed when a k-stretch crosses a deletion; these become q choices each and are constant per rule for fixed q. The record's k=2 ceil(log_q n)+2 still gives a constant-density k-unique family because two length-k windows agree with exact probability q^(-k), and L=3(k+1) preserves the shared-source argument. In the one-extra-component case, R>L>=log_q n gives n<=q^R; with fixed q this is absorbed into the per-rule polylogarithmic description factor. The remaining hash, witness, component and bipartition arguments are alphabet-independent integer-vector combinatorics. The claimed (2t-1)log_q n+O_{q,t}(log log n) bound follows.

limitations: The theorem is existential and assumes q and t fixed as n tends to infinity.
It does not improve the coefficient below 2t-1 or remove the O_{q,t}(log log n) term.
The proof is an adaptation of En Gad's binary method; the hashing and witness machinery are prior work.
The public priority window is only days wide, so simultaneous or not-yet-indexed work cannot be excluded.

originality.summary: En Gad's September 16, 2026 v1 explicitly asks whether the coefficient 2t-1 holds for codes over a fixed larger alphabet. Repository history shows this record was committed at 2026-09-18 04:23:02 UTC, before the later duplicate SCOPE record audited in the same assignment. Fresh searches through September 29 did not locate an external q-ary fixed-alphabet theorem with this coefficient. Earlier q-ary multiple-deletion constructions have larger leading redundancy. Originality is therefore supported only to the best of current public knowledge and is unusually exposed to simultaneous-work risk because the motivating question was only days old.

primary_source_check: En Gad arXiv:2609.19493v1 was retrieved in full after direct open-access fetch attempts failed. Section 8 explicitly lists fixed larger alphabets as open; Lemmas 2.6 and 5.1 were compared against the q-ary modifications.

scientific_value.summary: The theorem closes an explicit open extension in the motivating paper and shows that the one-power-of-n gain from random linear hashing is not binary-specific. For t=2 it lowers the existential fixed-q leading redundancy from the classical coefficient 4 to 3, while correctly leaving efficient construction and the sharp coefficient open.
